# Rivers return to the valley after forty dry years

![The river at dawn]
The river at dawn, seen from the old bridge.

For the first time in four decades, water is flowing through the **Ardent Valley** all year round. Engineers removed the last of three dams in the spring, and the river found its old bed within weeks.

"We expected it to take years," said hydrologist [Maria Okafor](/people/maria-okafor). "The valley remembered where the water should go."

## What changed

The dams were built in the 1980s to feed a reservoir that was never finished. A [2025 feasibility study](environment-agency.example.gov/reports/2025/ardent-valley-d…) found that removing them would cost less than repairing them.

> Rivers are patient. Give them a chance and they come back.

## What happens next

- Salmon counts start in March.
- The old reservoir site becomes a wetland park.
- Farmers downstream get a new water agreement, see [the agreement](#agreement).

The agreement runs for *twenty* years and is reviewed every five.
